item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 17, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's what's happening across the media industry.
The nominations are in for the 2027 Grammy Awards, with RAYE leading the field with 11 nods. ROSALÍA, Olivia Rodrigo, Bruno Mars, Taylor Swift and Ella Langley are among the artists competing in major categories, including Album, Record and Song of the Year. The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will air February 7 on ABC and stream on Disney Plus and Hulu. See the full list of nominees at Media Jobs Report dot com.
In radio news,
Detroit radio veteran “Big Jim” O’Brien has a new home on the dial. O’Brien is taking over weekday afternoons from 2 to 7 on Audacy’s 104.3 WOMC. He most recently spent 24 years hosting mornings at WCSX and has helped raise more than $3 million for Detroit-area charities during his career. O’Brien says Detroit is home and he’s excited to join the WOMC team.
Turning to television,
Sinclair Senior Vice President and WBFF General Manager Bill Fanshawe is retiring December 31st after more than 30 years with the company and nearly 40 years in television. Fanshawe has led Sinclair’s flagship Baltimore station while overseeing operations in several markets nationwide. Sinclair praised his leadership and mentorship of station managers throughout the company.
In podcasting news,
City Cast has named Co-Founder Andi McDaniel its new CEO, succeeding Founder David Plotz. The local media network has grown to 13 cities, reaching 1.5 million people through podcasts, newsletters, video and live events. McDaniel will focus on expanding audiences and revenue.
Turning to television,
The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade celebrates its historic 100th march November 26th, with performances from Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims, Queen Latifah, Jimmy Fallon and The Roots, and dozens more. The NBC and Peacock broadcast begins at 8:30 Thanksgiving morning, featuring a record 100 inflatable elements, new floats and the traditional arrival of Santa Claus. Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker return as hosts.
Recognizing achievement across the media industry,
BTS, *Spider-Man: Brand New Day* and *KPop Demon Hunters* were among the big winners at the 2026 Nickelodeon Kids’ Choice Awards. BTS picked up three awards, while Tom Holland, Zendaya and Jenna Ortega also took home honors. Hosted by Alex Warren, the CBS and Nickelodeon broadcast featured live performances, celebrity appearances and plenty of green slime. See the complete winners list at Media Jobs Report dot com.
Turning to radio,
WPLR morning hosts Chaz and AJ teamed up with WFSB Meteorologist Scot Haney for their annual "Three Men and a Box" fundraiser in Milford, Connecticut. The trio took on 24 hours of confinement, complete with a continuously repeating song, to raise money for local children. The fundraiser supported the December 11 Chaz and AJ Crabtree Motor Group Toy Drive.
In television news,
CNN en Español has named veteran international journalist Shery Ahn an Anchor and Correspondent, beginning January 4. Based in New York, Ahn will help expand the network’s business and economic reporting, focusing on issues affecting Hispanic communities, including jobs, affordability and personal finance. She joins CNN after nearly two decades of international journalism experience, most recently with Bloomberg Television in Tokyo.
Turning to streaming,
SiriusXM and Pandora are bringing Keith Urban to New York City for an exclusive holiday concert on December eighth at Hammerstein Ballroom. The country superstar will perform career hits and holiday favorites. The concert airs December eighteenth at 8 p.m. Eastern on SiriusXM's The Highway, Channel 56. Fans can enter online for a chance to attend.
And finally,
TNA Wrestling and iHeartRadio are teaming up to launch TNA Wrestling Radio later this year. The exclusive digital station will feature classic matches, pay-per-views, interviews and memorable moments from TNA's more than 20-year library. Original podcasts, celebrity shows and exclusive interviews are planned for 2027, including a podcast dedicated to the Knockouts Division.
Stay current with more media news, the latest jobs and free industry tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
